calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-1-prob: Differentiate the circular position: v is perpendicular to r and a=−ω²r. The inward force magnitude is mRω²=mv²/R.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-2-prob: Divide Fsinθ=mv²/R by Fcosθ=mg. At fixed banking angle, R scales as v²;1.5²×400=900.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-3-prob: Eliminate t to get y=x tanα−x²(1+tan²α)/(2R); real roots in tanα give the reachable envelope. Shared gravitational drop proves interception.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-4-prob: Intersect the projectile with y=±x tanθ. Along-plane range is2v0² cosα sin(α±θ)/(g cos²θ); optimize the sine product. For uphill target distance R the optimal v0²=Rg(1+sinθ).
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-5-prob: Use g32ft/s² and initial vertical speed0. Rebound components both scale by0.8, so its additional horizontal range is(2·0.8)(2·0.8|vy|/32)=1.28 times the first horizontal distance.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-6-prob: By the fundamental theorem, r′=(sin(πt²/2),cos(πt²/2)) has unit speed. Its derivative has magnitudeπ|t|.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-7-prob: Integrate speed over the full flight: S=(v²/g)[sinα+cos²α asinh(tanα)]. The unique interior maximum occurs near56.47°, which rounds to56°; this differs from maximum horizontal range.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-8-prob: Unroll the centerline cylinder of circumference C=2π(R+r). A helix of axial pitch p has perpendicular spacing pC/sqrt(C²+p²). Equating that spacing to2r gives p=2rC/sqrt(C²−4r²). The axial span of centerline length L is Lp/sqrt(C²+p²)=2rL/C=Lr/[π(R+r)]. For r≪R this becomes Lr/(πR). This is the elementary unrolled-strip winding model, with end effects and exact3D solid-tube contact explicitly excluded.
calculus-chapter-13-problems-plus-9-prob: Dot the displacement with a×b. If this normal vanishes, choose any nonzero normal perpendicular to the remaining span instead.
